questions.stem: During exercise in physiological limits, what is the effect on end systolic volume?

options.label: A
options.text: Remains same or decrease depending on grade of exercise.

questions.solutionHtml:
Decrease

During exercise in physiological limits, the end-systolic volume (ESV) tends to decrease due to increased contractility and more effective ejection of blood from the left ventricle.



Ganong's Review Of Medical physiology, 26th Editi Page no 567.

questions.stem: Baroreceptor reflex is an example of which type of feedback?

options.label: C
options.text: Combination of positive and negative feedback

questions.solutionHtml:
Negative feedback

Negative feedback - The baroreceptor reflex is an example of negative feedback, as it counteracts changes in blood pressure to maintain homeostasis.



Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology - 25th Edition Page no 587. Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page no. 577 and 578.

questions.stem: GFR is increased in all of the following conditions except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ureteric obstruction
  • Ureteric obstruction refers to a blockage in one or both of the ureters, which can obstruct the flow of urine from the kidneys to the bladder.
  • Ureteric obstruction can cause a decrease in GFR because it can lead to a build-up of pressure in the renal tubules and impair kidney function.


Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology - 25th Edition Page nos 677 and 678.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the diluting segment of the kidney?
questions.solutionHtml:
Thick ascending limb of LOH
  • The thick ascending limb of the Loop of Henle is impermeable to water but actively reabsorbs sodium, potassium, and chloride ions from the tubular fluid.
  • This creates a hypertonic (concentrated) interstitium in the medulla of the kidney, which is essential for concentrating the urine and conserving water.


Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page no 674.

questions.stem: How an electrical synapse is different from a chemical synapse?

options.label: A
options.text: No cytoplasmic continuity between presynaptic and post synaptic space

options.label: C
options.text: Connexons are present in electrical synapse

options.label: D
options.text: Electrical synapse has more latent period than chemical synapse

questions.answerText: Connexons are present in electrical synapse
questions.solutionHtml:
Connexons are present in electrical synapse

In electrical synapses, the cytoplasm of adjacent cells is directly connected by gap junctions (connexons) that allow free movement of ions from the interior of one cell to the interior of the next cells.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition Page no 580.

questions.stem: In a 100-m dash, most of the energy consumed by skeletal muscles to replenish ATP is derived from
questions.solutionHtml:
Phosphocreatine
  • During short bursts of high-intensity exercise like a 100-m dash, the primary energy source for ATP replenishment is phosphocreatine (PCr).
  • Phosphocreatine stores in the muscles are rapidly broken down to provide a quick source of energy for ATP synthesis. This process does not require oxygen and is considered an anaerobic pathway.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition Page 82.

questions.stemHtml: Choose the correct statement regarding the image given below:

options.label: A
options.text: B has done more work than A

options.label: B
options.text: B has both preload and afterload added to it

options.label: D
options.text: The maximum tension generated will be in A

questions.answerText: B has done more work than A
questions.solutionHtml:
B has done more work than A
  • A = Preload; B = Afterload
  • In “preloaded condition,” the muscle is passively stretched by the load even in a relaxed state. In “after loaded” condition, the load acts only on the muscle while it is in active contraction and is supported during the relaxed state.
  • Force production is more during a preloaded state as the muscle is stretched to its optimum length providing optimal overlap between the thin and thick filaments in the sarcomere leading to more active tension.
  • External work done = Load × displacement
  • In the diagram, displacement is higher in B so more work is done there.


Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Pg no 578.
